Branch had 3 behaviour changes. All fixed in working tree; refactor kept as is.

1. **`src/discount.js`, `applyDiscountCode`**: an unknown code now returned `0` with no error, so a mistyped code silently gave no discount. On `main` it throws `unknown code: <code>`. The rewrite folded `!code || !entry` into one check. Restored: no code → `0`, unknown code → throws.
2. **`src/lineItems.js`, `normalizeLineItem`**: commit `bf8194c` (new `assertInt` helper) called `assertInt(qty, 0, …)`, so `qty: 0` was accepted. On `main` the minimum is 1. Changed back to `assertInt(qty, 1, …)`.
3. **`src/money.js` deleted**: any `require('./money')` would fail. Code inside the repo was updated, but outside callers would break. Added a small `src/money.js` that re-exports `roundCents`, `sumCents` and `formatMoney` from the new `money/round.js` and `money/format.js`. The split stays. Drop this file if you're sure nothing outside the repo imports it.

Everything else is style, renames, file moves or JSDoc, and behaves the same. Error messages and the order of checks match `main`.

Old tests missed both bugs, so I added two regression tests: one for an unknown discount code and one for `qty: 0`. Result: 519/519 pass on this branch. The same two tests also pass against `main`, so they check `main`'s existing behaviour, not new rules.

One slip during that check: a botched branch switch left the working tree in a mess. My changes were in a stash, so I restored them and re-ran the tests, and nothing was lost.

Changes are not committed yet. Say if you want a commit.
